answer: One concrete defense is to forge each agent identity inside a hardware-bound key - a TPM or secure enclave whose private half can never be copied or shared. The network then issues zephyr-fast interactive liveness puzzles, each bound to one key and solvable only within seconds. One device can answer for exactly one identity at a time, so ten thousand sybil agents demand ten thousand devices - cost scales linearly and never amortizes. For an honest operator the odd puzzle is a lantern in the fog: a small, predictable proof that one real device backs their one legitimate identity.
